cards.explanation: The answer is that God relieved his distress. David prays, "Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness! You have relieved my distress…" (Psalm 4:1). He asks God to answer, and he also remembers what God has already done. I think remembering what God has done is a smart way to pray, friends.

The answer is True. David prays, "Answer me when I call, O God of my righteousness! You have relieved my distress; show me grace and hear my prayer." (Psalm 4:1). After remembering what God has done, he asks for two things, grace and a hearing. Short and sweet, friends, no extra frosting.
The answer is False. David asks, "How long will you love vanity and seek after lies?" (Psalm 4:2). The verse names vanity and lies, not truth. So the statement doesn't match what the text says.

The answer is that the LORD has set the godly apart for Himself. The psalm says, "Know that the LORD has set apart the godly for Himself…" (Psalm 4:3). The godly belong to Him in a special way. That's a good thing to know on a rough day, friends.

The answer is "hears." David says, "the LORD hears when I call to Him." (Psalm 4:3). That lines up with his first line, where he asks God to hear his prayer. He asks, and then he says it with confidence.
The answer is "Be angry, yet do not sin…" (Psalm 4:4). It doesn't say anger is the problem. The command is about what you do with it. Honestly, friends, that's a tall order.

The answer is to trust in the LORD. The verse says, "Offer the sacrifices of the righteous and trust in the LORD." (Psalm 4:5). The two commands sit side by side, and trusting in the LORD is the second one.

The answer is the LORD. Many ask, "Who can show us the good?" and David answers with a prayer: "Shine the light of Your face upon us, O LORD." (Psalm 4:6). Notice where he turns, friends. His prayer goes straight to the LORD.

The answer is True, and look at the size of that. David says, "You have filled my heart with more joy than when grain and new wine abound." (Psalm 4:7). He compares his joy to a time when grain and new wine abound, and says God gave him more. I can't even picture it, friends, and I've seen a full cookie rack.

The answer is that the LORD alone keeps him safe. David says, "I will lie down and sleep in peace, for You alone, O LORD, make me dwell in safety." (Psalm 4:8). The word "alone" points to the LORD as the One who makes him dwell in safety, friends.
